title: 3.7L Cooling System: Reading the Component Map
introduction:
I read this cooling diagram like a heat-delivery route: the pump moves coolant through the engine, the radiator passes heat to outside air, and the heater core puts some of that heat to work in the cabin. It covers the 3.7L Duratec arrangement.

Start at the coolant pump beside the engine, follow the arrows through the block and cylinder heads, then trace the radiator and heater branches. The radiator is drawn on the right, the heater core on the lower left, and the degas bottle below the engine. Match each callout to the table; the separated components show connections rather than a literal underhood arrangement. LH and RH identify the left-hand and right-hand cylinder heads.

The upper and lower radiator hoses connect the radiator circuit to the engine-side plumbing and thermostat housing. The heater inlet hose feeds the heater core; its outlet hose and tube lead back through the coolant return route. The degas bottle provides expansion space and helps remove air, with separate connections shown to the thermostat housing and radiator. Follow arrowheads for direction and use their colors with the temperature note below.

This map identifies components, connections and illustrated temperature bands. It is not an overheating test, hose-removal guide or set of pass/fail temperature limits.

edits.text: NOTE: Coolant temperature changes with ambient temperature and engine load. This illustration represents an ambient temperature of 38° C (100° F). Red arrows show coolant over 90° C (194° F), Orange arrows show coolant at approximately 90° C (194° F), and Blue arrows show coolant below 90° C (194° F).
edits.why: Arrowheads show the route; color shows the illustrated temperature band. The cooler arrows appear turquoise in the drawing. These bands explain the picture under its stated conditions and should not be used alone to condemn a thermostat, pump or radiator.
